summary: Three Terra agents implemented and tested checkpointing and purity-aware warm initialization in parallel; root integrated them into the Group 2 runner. Short real-data smoke runs did not produce a nonempty national plan. No speedup or resolution of the original timeouts is claimed.

scope.purity: Unchanged for N, WH and FI
scope.geography: Unchanged; only the existing WA=1200 override remains

implementation.initializer_method: Bounded auxiliary HiGHS MILP with explicit binary state-channel purity selectors and the first nonzero coverage objective. A returned point is stripped to the original variable layout and checked for finite values, integrality and every original model constraint before use.
implementation.fallback: No valid seed means the original solver runs cold. No constraint is relaxed and no pass is skipped.
implementation.checkpoint_method: Atomic JSON containing validated full vectors and model/input/source fingerprints. Save after a validated seed and after each returned engine pass. Root/flow variables are reconstructed and checked when the solver returns only z/y.
implementation.resume_method: Compatible checkpoints provide warm starts for fresh optimization. They are not certificates and do not skip previous objectives or stages.
implementation.progress: stage_progress.json records seed status, per-pass termination, objectives, available dual bounds and node counts, timing, and checkpoint locations.
implementation.isolation: Scenario-level hooks are restored on failure. Pre-existing user changes in core planning and staffing files were not edited or committed.

usage.ceiling_case: Use --count-mode cap with a separate fresh output directory.
usage.reuse: Add --resume-checkpoints PREVIOUS_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY/checkpoints. Both the model and provenance must match; changed source hashes reject reuse.
usage.baseline: Use --seed-time-limit 0 to disable the auxiliary initializer. Checkpointing remains enabled.

tests.typecheck: Pyright: 0 errors and 0 warnings on all three implementation modules
tests.full_suite: 909 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped with TD_GAZ_VINTAGE=2025, the hub 2025 TD_ZCTA_SHP, and pipefail preserving the runner exit status
coverage: Pure-state assignment, permitted same-channel district splitting and exact counts
Auxiliary variables do not leak into the original solver model
Finite/integral/full-constraint validation, invalid priors and no-seed fallback
Corrupt/stale checkpoints and fractional pure allocations rejected
Cross-process fingerprint and connected-flow checkpoint roundtrip
Seed checkpoint survives failure before the first engine solve
Engine and planner hooks restored after failures
Test environment restored after mocked CLI failure
tests.serena: Unavailable because no active project or activation tool is exposed; read-only rg/sed and Pyright used instead.

fixed.main_solver: No incumbent before first national coverage timeout

cap.main_solver: Only empty national incumbents within the short coverage budgets; rejected as an incomplete plan
cap.verdict: Inconclusive, not a successful territory plan

real_data_smokes.provenance: Each run_request.json records loaded source/input hashes. Final type-safety changes and seed-before-first-pass checkpointing landed after smoke launch; focused tests cover those final changes.

limitations: No complete territory plan, realized ZIP assignment, staffing comparison or FEFx audit was produced.
The short smoke budgets do not establish whether the initializer improves production-budget performance.
Checkpointing preserves returned pass results and validated seeds, not every live incumbent during a running pass.
The underlying sequential planner still cannot reconsider national choices after downstream WH/FI failure; cross-channel repair or joint solving is not implemented here.

HiGHS thread count remains process-global. Production Group 2 launches use a fresh process with two threads; live-solver tests use fresh processes to avoid contamination from unrelated suite settings.
followups: Compare seeded and cold runs at matched wall-clock budgets, then tune seed versus main-search time based on time to first nonempty incumbent.
If national allocations still leave WH/FI without usable plans, implement a separately tested cross-channel repair or seeded joint workflow rather than silently relaxing purity or opportunity bounds.
learned: level0.check_point does not reject NaN by itself; checkpoint and seed boundaries explicitly require finite vectors.
Changing the thread count after a HiGHS pool is initialized can invalidate a solve. The auxiliary and production paths now use the same highspy thread setting.
A full-suite pipeline needs pipefail or a captured runner exit code; filter success alone is not a test pass.
